title: India Lost to Ireland. The Rain Stole Chester-le-Street. Old Trafford on Saturday Is Where Iyer's Team Has to Start Answering.
excerpt: Varun Chakaravarthy's return, Sooryavanshi's wait, and a hostile England side await India in the second T20I at Manchester.
body:
The rain took everything. India had scored 189 for 7, Abhishek Sharma had blazed 59 off 24 balls to become the fastest player to 100 T20I sixes, Shreyas Iyer had ground out a captain's 68, Shivam Dube had smashed an unbeaten 42 — and none of it counted. The first T20I at Chester-le-Street was abandoned without a ball bowled in England's reply.

The series is level at 0-0. The stakes, however, have not diminished. India head to Old Trafford on Saturday for the second T20I carrying the weight of a shock 2-0 series defeat in Ireland and a washed-out opener that denied them the chance to answer their critics.

## The Ireland Hangover

India's recent form is, to put it gently, concerning. The 2-0 whitewash at the hands of Ireland — a team ranked outside the top eight — exposed a brittle top order and a bowling unit that looked short of ideas. Shreyas Iyer's appointment as T20I captain was supposed to signal a new era after India's World Cup triumph in March. So far, that era has produced two defeats, a washout, and a growing list of questions.


![Shreyas Iyer — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ae/Shreyas_Iyer_snapped_at_the_airport_%28Cropped%29.jpg)


Chief among them: the all-rounder void. Hardik Pandya is in Bengaluru rehabilitating at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. Nitish Kumar Reddy has been ruled out with an injury. Suryansh Shedge, drafted as emergency cover, debuted in Ireland but failed to make an impression.

## Chakaravarthy Returns, Sooryavanshi Waits



> **"So far, that era has produced two defeats, a washout, and a growing list of questions."**


The biggest selection talking point is Varun Chakaravarthy. The mystery spinner missed the Ireland series while completing a rehab for a foot injury sustained during the IPL. He has now joined the squad in England and, if declared fit, is expected to replace Shedge in the playing XI at Old Trafford.

Then there is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old prodigy whose selection in the squad made global headlines. India have indicated they are in no hurry to hand him a debut, and the Chester-le-Street washout delayed any decision further. The left-handed opener scored 55 off 31 balls for Rajasthan Royals in this year's IPL and has been spoken of as India's next generational talent. Old Trafford on a Saturday afternoon, against an England attack featuring Saqib Mahmood and Adil Rashid, would be a baptism by fire.


![Shivam Dube — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/63/Shivam_Dube_in_PMO_New_Delhi.jpg)


The probable Indian XI: Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan (wk), Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav, Varun Chakaravarthy.

## England Are Not Messing Around

Harry Brook's England are treating this series as a statement of intent. The hosts named a 17-man squad two days after the conclusion of the Trent Bridge Test against New Zealand, with Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue rested but Saqib Mahmood recalled. Mahmood took 3 for 33 in the washed-out first T20I, consistently hitting 90 mph and troubling India's middle order.

Phil Salt, Jos Buttler, Jacob Bethell and Sam Curran give England depth and firepower across the batting order. Adil Rashid remains their trump card in the middle overs. And Brook, who scored over 600 runs in this year's IPL for Sunrisers Hyderabad, captains with an aggression that mirrors his batting.


![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)


England's playing XI from Chester-le-Street: Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (wk), Harry Brook (c), Jacob Bethell, Tom Banton, Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Liam Dawson, Adil Rashid, Luke Wood, Saqib Mahmood.

## Old Trafford and the Diaspora

Manchester is home to one of the largest Indian and Pakistani communities in the United Kingdom. The curry mile of Rusholme, barely three miles from Old Trafford, has been a cornerstone of South Asian life in England for decades. When India play at this ground, the crowd splits into a sea of blue jerseys and English whites, and the atmosphere carries the energy of a festival.

Saturday's match begins at 2:30 PM local time (6:30 AM Pacific, 9:30 AM Eastern, 7 PM IST). For NRIs across the UK, it is a rare Saturday afternoon fixture — no late-night alarm needed, no Monday-morning fog. The timing alone should fill Old Trafford to its 19,000-seat capacity.

## What's at Stake

India cannot afford another slow start. The Ireland defeat, the top-order collapses, and the absence of a genuine pace-bowling all-rounder have all been dissected at length. If the rain stays away in Manchester, this is the match where Iyer's captaincy — and India's white-ball direction ahead of the 2028 T20 World Cup — begins to take shape.

The five-match T20I series continues in Nottingham (July 7), Bristol (July 9), and Southampton (July 11), followed by three ODIs. But Old Trafford is where the tone gets set.

Or reset.
